Human: What are the common causes of overcooked rice?

Assistant: That question has been asked many times. Here are the answers we’ve found to be the most useful so far. "Cooking the rice" is a very simplified view. In reality there are many causes, including the kind of rice being used, the type of pot or pan being used, if the rice is adding to a hot dish, adding to a cold main course, etc. One of the most common causes of overcooked rice is the ratio between the liquid and the starchy part of the grain (the ratio of water to rice).  The ratio varies depending on the kind of rice.  Brown, long-grain rice will take much longer to cook than short-grain or sushi rice. The same is true of wild and premium (unpasteurized) rice versus pasteurized rice. Another major factor is if you are adding the rice to a hot or cold dish.  If you add the rice to a cold dish after it has completely cooled, then you risk taking forever to cook the rice. On the other hand adding the rice to a hot dish before the dish is assembled can lead to undercooked rice as well. 
A good rule of thumb is to only add the rice to a hot dish once the dish is about to be served anyway. That way you have at least an hour or more to cook the rice.
"Starchy part of the grain" is another way of saying "flour or other starch." Since the starchy part of the grain is what gives your breads and pastries their starchiness, you want to avoid getting the rice too starchy and mushy. 
Another common cause of overcooked rice is to have a timer or electronic timer that can’t reach the end of the pot of rice. This can happen when the pot of rice is in an area where there are a lot of electronic devices.
